title: Reduction of Carbonyl Compounds
author: 3iGR44tcGMnRnhEYm
chapter_outcomes: Recall the reactions (reagents and conditions) by which aldehydes and ketones can be produced: (a) the oxidation of primary alcohols using acidified $\mathrm{K_2 Cr_2 O_7}$ or acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and distillation to produce aldehydes (b) the oxidation of secondary alcohols using acidified $\mathrm{K_2 Cr_2 O_7}$ or acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and distillation to produce ketones

Describe the reduction of aldehydes and ketones using $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ or $\mathrm{LiAl H_4}$ to produce alcohols, and the reaction of aldehydes and ketones with $\mathrm{HCN}$, $\mathrm{KCN}$ as catalyst, and heat to produce hydroxynitriles as exemplified by ethanal and propanone
Describe the mechanism of the nucleophilic addition reactions of hydrogen cyanide with aldehydes and ketones
Describe the use of 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine ($\mathrm{2,4-DNPH}$ reagent) to detect the presence of carbonyl compounds
Deduce the nature (aldehyde or ketone) of an unknown carbonyl compound from the results of simple tests (Fehling’s and Tollens’ reagents; ease of oxidation)

Deduce the presence of a $\mathrm{CH_3 CO –}$ group in an aldehyde or ketone, $\mathrm{CH_3 CO–R}$, from its reaction with alkaline $\mathrm{I_2(aq)}$ to form a yellow precipitate of tri-iodomethane and an ion, $\mathrm{RCO_2 ^-}$
